expectr 0.1.0

Pipeline checkpoints for data expectations.

Statistical production code lives or dies on small assumptions: no duplicate units, no negative amounts, no person with two addresses at once. expectr turns each assumption into one line in the pipeline that warns or stops the moment it breaks, and shows the rows that broke it.

The pattern is always the same: express the rule as “the set of violations must be empty”, build that set with ordinary dplyr, and pass it to a checkpoint.

library(expectr)

sales |>
  expect_none(is.na(customer_id), abort_msg = "Sales without a customer id") |>
  expect_none(amount < 0, warn_msg = "Negative amounts") |>
  expect_unique(order_id)

Installation

expectr is not on CRAN. Install it from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("dataniel/expectr")

Functions

Function Description
expect_empty() The violation set you pipe in has no rows
expect_none() No row matches a condition; returns the full data for chaining
expect_unique() Key columns identify each row uniquely
expect_balanced() Every unit observed in every period, or no gaps (gaps_only)
expect_no_overlap() Spells (addresses, employment) do not overlap within a unit
tally_violations() Count violations for many rules at once; judges nothing
flag_duplicates() Prepend isdup/dupid columns to mark duplicate rows
view_types() Compare column types across data frames; does it bind?

Every checkpoint can append a line to a log and write the offending rows to a CSV file, set once per script with options(expectr.log = ..., expectr.dump = ...). A failure signals a condition of class expectr_failure that carries the rows.

Built for registers

The checkpoints are built for full-population registers. In memory they group character keys such as cpr in one linear pass instead of sorting them, and check a million persons over five years in under a second (see benchmarks/). A DuckDB or Arrow table is checked in the database, without loading it into R:

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "register.duckdb")

dplyr::tbl(con, "persons") |>
  expect_unique(cpr, year) |>
  expect_balanced(cpr, year, gaps_only = TRUE)

Origin

The checkpoints started in daos, which re-exports them, so existing scripts keep working.
